title: Regina Spektor Opens Children’s & Family Emmys With ‘Won’t You Be My Neighbor?’ Cover: Full Winners List
summary: Descendants: The Rise of Red -- the fourth installment in the Disney Channel movie musical series -- picked up five prizes Monday night.
contentText:
The award for “most wholesome awards show” goes to the fourth annual Children’s & Family Emmys.

On Monday night, The National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences announced the winners of the Children’s and Family Emmy Awards at Jazz at Lincoln Center’s Frederick P. Rose Hall in New York.

Singer/songwriter Regina Spektor opened the ceremony with a cover of the iconic Mr. Rogers’ Neighborhood theme song “Won’t You Be My Neighbor?” Performing alone onstage, Spektor accompanied herself on piano. As she sang the first lines, Spektor received applause from the audience as they recognized the song. Spektor concluded her performance with a “Hello, neighbor!” directed to the crowd.

Actor, director and puppeteer John Tartaglia hosted the event, as stars like Amber Riley ( Glee ), Rachel Accurso (aka Ms. Rachel), Monique Coleman ( High School Musical ) and Bill Nye presented the night’s awards. Awardees included actor Joe Locke, who won outstanding lead performer for his role in Heartstopper ; Tabitha Brown in the outstanding children’s personality category for Tab Time ; and John Lithgow for his voice performance in Spellbound .

Two music awards were handed out at the Children’s & Family Emmy Awards: The award for outstanding music direction and composition for a live action program was awarded to the BYUtv series Secrets at Red Rocks for the episode “Open Your Mind a Little.” Meanwhile, the AppleTV program WondLa won in the outstanding music direction and composition for an animated program category for the episode “Heart.” In addition, Descendants: The Rise of Red — the fourth installment in the popular Disney Channel movie musical series — picked up five prizes Monday night, including for outstanding fiction special.
